original_value: Congestive heart failure (CHF) poses a serious threat to human health. Once the diagnosis of CHF is established, clinical experts need to assess the severity of CHF in a timely manner. It is proved that electrocardiogram (ECG) signals are useful for assessing the severity of CHF. However, since the ECG perturbations are subtle, it is difficult for doctors to detect the differences of ECGs. In order to help doctors to make an accurate diagnosis, we proposed a novel multi-scale residual network (ResNet) to automatically classify CHF into four classifications according to the New York Heart Association (NYHA) functional classification system. Furthermore, in order to make the reported results more realistic, we used an inter-patient paradigm to divide the dataset, and segmented the ECG signals into two different intervals. The experimental results show that the proposed multi-scale ResNet-34 has achieved an average positive predictive value, sensitivity and accuracy of 93.49%, 93.44% and 93.60% respectively for two seconds of ECG segments. We have also obtained an average positive predictive value, sensitivity and accuracy of 94.16%, 93.79% and 94.29% respectively for five seconds of ECG segments. The proposed method can be used as an auxiliary tool to help doctors to classify CHF.

result.paraphrase: Congestive heart failure (CHF) is a major threat to human health. After CHF is diagnosed, clinicians must promptly evaluate its severity. Electrocardiogram (ECG) signals have been shown to be useful for this purpose, but the ECG changes are subtle, making them difficult for doctors to distinguish. To support accurate diagnosis, we proposed a new multi-scale residual network (ResNet) that automatically classifies CHF into four categories based on the New York Heart Association (NYHA) functional classification system. In addition, to make the reported performance more realistic, we adopted an inter-patient paradigm for dataset splitting and divided the ECG signals into two segment lengths. Experimental results indicate that the proposed multi-scale ResNet-34 achieved average positive predictive value, sensitivity, and accuracy of 93.49%, 93.44%, and 93.60%, respectively, for two-second ECG segments. For five-second ECG segments, the corresponding averages were 94.16%, 93.79%, and 94.29%. This method can serve as an auxiliary tool to help doctors classify CHF.
